- Correctness first; then maintainability 6 months out.
- Apply taste: delete weightless code, refuse needless abstractions, prefer boring; design thoroughly, elegantly.
- Consider compiled code: NEVER avoidably allocate, copy, or compute.
- Unexpected repo changes: user's work; adapt.

# Skills & Rules
# Internal URLs
Most FS/bash tools auto-resolve these to FS paths.
- `rule://<name>`: details
- `agent://<id>`: output artifact; `/<child>`: nested-subagent output; otherwise `/<path>`: JSON field
- `history://<id>`: read-only agent transcript (live|parked|released); bare `history://`: all agents. Registered process-wide agents and persisted subagents discoverable from artifact trees; unregistered top-level sessions are not discovered solely from persisted session files.

- Read: `read`
- Grep: `grep`
- Glob: `glob`
- Web Search: `web_search`
- Submit Result: `yield`
§ Tool Policy
# General
Use tools when they improve correctness, completeness, or grounding.
- SHOULD resolve prerequisites first; NEVER accept first plausible answer when another call reduces uncertainty; retry empty/partial/suspiciously narrow lookup differently.
- SHOULD parallelize independent calls.
# Tool I/O
- Prefer relative `path`-like fields.
- Most tools take `i`: capitalized 2–6-word present-participle intent (e.g. "Reading model role settings").
# Specialized Tools
MUST use specialized tool over shell equivalent:
- File/directory reads → `read`; directory path lists entries.
- Regex search/target location → `grep`, not shell `grep`, `rg`, `awk`.
- Structure mapping/globbing → `glob`, not `ls **/*.ext` or `fd`.

NEVER open files hoping. AVOID unneeded files/sections.

# 1. Scope

# 4. Implement

# 5. Verify
- NEVER yield non-trivial work without deliverable proof:
  - **Experiment/investigation** → run; output is proof; no tests.
  - **UI change** → verify against the actual surface:
    - **TUI/CLI** → launch the actual program and verify terminal interaction, output, or state.
    - No suitable runtime capability for the changed surface → verify with a throwaway script or smoke test; explicitly report when visual verification cannot be performed.
  - **Bug fix** → reproduce, fix, confirm reproduction no longer triggers. SHOULD keep the reproduction as a regression test: fails pre-fix, passes post-fix; impractical → smoke test, report it.
  - **Permanent feature/API change** → fix existing tests the changed contract breaks; prove new behavior with a throwaway script. New test ONLY for a genuinely uncertain edge case, or on user request.
- Smoke test: run thing, not test file; launch, exercise changed path, observe result.
- Tests: permanent load, not proof of work. A test earns its place ONLY where a plausible bug would fail it.

  - Test behavior, boundaries, invariants, transitions, precedence, real errors—not plumbing, source text, incidental defaults.

  - NEVER write a test so the change "has tests" → throwaway script.
  - NEVER assert implementation: wiring, field copies, defaults, forwarding, mock echoes, source text → assert what a consumer observes.

Last phase; REQUIRED after smoke test proves work; NEVER pre-plan/pre-allocate cleanup todos.

# Scholar plan: one-pass review layer and runaway-loop prevention

For the implementing AI. Follow the phases in order. Each step names the exact files, the change and the test that proves it. Do not skip tests. Do not install until the whole suite passes.

## 0. Ground rules

- Working copy: `C:\Users\basam\Documents\Codex\2026-09-09\w\outputs\pi-scholar-loading-progress` (branch `feat/loading-progress`).
- Installed copy: `C:\Users\basam\.pi\agent\extensions\scholar` (branch `main`). Change it only in Phase 6, by fast-forwarding from the working copy.
- Node: `C:\Users\basam\AppData\Local\pi-node\current\node.exe`. Full suite: `node tests/run.mjs` (currently 55 verifiers, all must pass). One verifier: `node tests/<file>.mjs`.
- TypeScript baseline: from `...\w` run `node <npx-cache>/typescript/lib/tsc.js -p outputs/scholar-next-release-tsconfig.json --pretty false`. It must still report exactly the 55 existing diagnostics (compare with `outputs/scholar-052-types-final.log` after removing `(line,col)`).
- Never write to the real vault (`C:\Users\basam\Desktop\Basam's_Vault`) in tests. Tests use temporary copies.
- Do not change the teaching guidance (`TEACHING_ENGINE_POLICY`, `EXPLANATION_POLICY` in `policies.ts`). The user deferred that.
- Stay provider-neutral: use `ctx.model`, `ctx.modelRegistry` and `ctx.thinkingLevel`. Never switch the user's model or reasoning level.
- Commit messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not push to GitHub unless the user asks.

## 1. Current state (0.5.4, commit `4141149`)

| Area | Where | Today |
|---|---|---|
| Learn review | `learn-review.ts` (`planReviewAssignments`, `reviewLearnDraft`, `reviewOne`) | Parallel crew: source windows, one check per topic, visual packets, one coherence check. `REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6` |
| Checkpoints | `tool-controller.ts` (`saveReviewCheckpoints`) | Each passing check saved immediately; reused by exact packet key |
| Approval gate | `learn-quality.ts` (`reviewGateIssues`), `lesson.ts` (`learnReviewIssues`, `lessonReady`) | Every role must pass on the current lesson hash, so any fix forces re-review |
| Round and attempt limits | `tool-controller.ts` | `MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS = 3`, `MAX_PREREVIEW_REJECTIONS = 4`, sticky stop latch (`stoppedDelivery`) |
| Clocks | `tool-controller.ts` `LEARN_WORK_LIMIT_MS`, `MIN_REVIEW_WINDOW_MS`; `runtime-coordinator.ts` interval in `ensureScholarTurnInputLock`; `review-runtime.ts` `DEFAULT_REVIEWER_LIMITS.timeoutMs` (12 min) | Hard wall-clock stops |
| Output cap | `learn-review.ts` `reviewOne` limits: `maxOutputTokens: Math.min(32_000, ...)` | DeepSeek at max reasoning hit it on every check |
| Question review | `learn-review.ts` `reviewLearnQuestion`; called from `tool-controller.ts` `reviewQuestion` and `index.ts` `tool_call` hook | Learn only |
| Tutor | none | No review |
| Exam | `exam.ts` `validateExamQuestions`, `examFormIssues` | Code rules only, no review |
| Exam callouts | `render/assessment.ts` `examAnswerNoteText`, `gradedQuestionLines`; `exam.ts` `parseExamResponses` | Already done: every paper question and answer region sits inside `> [!question]`; the parser accepts `> `-framed regions; the answer key uses callouts |
| Pi tools during modes | `runtime-coordinator.ts` `syncActiveTools` | Keeps Pi's `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit` on. A DeepSeek author used `bash` to list the home folder |

## 2. Goals

1. One review pass per target, then done. No review/rewrite cycles.
2. The same small review layer for Learn, Tutor and Exam.
3. Works with any Pi model: any output limit, any context size, with or without images, with imperfect JSON.
4. No runaway loops, enforced by counts and progress detection rather than wall clocks.
5. Exam papers keep questions in callouts and keep the submit flow byte-for-byte compatible.

## 3. The review layer (shared by all modes)

### 3.1 Packet

Rename `ReviewAssignment` to `ReviewPacket` and move the generic runner into a new `review-layer.ts`. `learn-review.ts` keeps only Learn's planner.

```ts
type ReviewPacket = {
  role: "source" | "teaching" | "visual" | "assessment";
  id: string;                 // unique within one pass
  instruction: string;        // scoped task
  reads: number[]; views: number[]; cropIds: string[];
  payload: Record<string, unknown>;  // only this packet's passages
};
```

`runReviewPass(options, packets)` does exactly what `reviewLearnDraft` does today: pool of `REVIEW_CONCURRENCY` workers, packet-key cache, `onCheckpoint`, one aggregate receipt per role. Keep `reviewOne` as the single-packet runner.

### 3.2 One-pass flow (every mode)

```
author writes -> code validators -> ONE review pass -> author answers every blocking finding -> commit
```

- **Finding key.** Compute, don't store: `findingKey = sha256(role + "\u0000" + target + "\u0000" + issue).slice(0, 12)`. The review result shows each finding as `[F-<key>]`. No change to the `ReviewFinding` schema.
- **Author response.** New optional `findingResponses: Array<{ key: string; action: "fixed" | "declined"; note: string }>` on `notes` (Learn and Tutor) and `exam_build` (Exam). Add it to `tool-contract.ts` `ScholarParams`. `note` must be 1–600 characters.
- **Commit rule.** Commit when:
  - a completed pass exists for this target (any content hash), and
  - every blocking finding from that pass has a response, and
  - the code validators pass on the current content.

  Never run a second pass for the same target in the same activation.
- **Execution failures.** A packet that fails (provider error, timeout, output limit, malformed verdict) is retried once, within the same pass. If it fails again, the pass completes anyway, and the commit adds a visible warning, for example `> [!warning] Not independently reviewed: visual (provider error)`.
- **Storage.**
  - Learn: keep receipts in `learnQuality.reviews`, and add `learnQuality.responses?: FindingResponse[]`.
  - Tutor: add `review?: { version: 1; receipts: ReviewReceipt[]; responses: FindingResponse[] }` on `TutorSession`.
  - Exam: add the same field on `ScholarExam`.
  - Validate all three in `state-schema.ts`, updating `hasOnlyKeys` lists and adding an `isFindingResponse` guard in `learn-quality.ts`.
- **Legacy.** Sections already approved under the old gate stay approved. `lessonReady` accepts either the old receipts or the new one-pass record.

### 3.3 Packets per mode

| Mode | Trigger | Packets | Blocks until done? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Learn lesson | `notes.lessonComplete` | Existing crew (`planReviewAssignments`), unchanged | Yes |
| Learn/Tutor question | new graded question (`assess` pending, `scholar_quiz`) | 1 `assessment` packet (question + its source pages + crops) | Yes |
| Tutor explanation | first `notes.lesson` save of a unit | 1 `teaching` packet: that unit's markdown + its `sourcePages` text. At most 1 per unit | Yes, one request only |
| Exam form | `exam_build` | 1 `assessment` packet per question (question, key, rubric, its source pages) + 1 `teaching` packet for the whole form (coverage, balance, cues across questions; no source text) | Yes, before freezing |
| Exam grading | `exam_grade` | none (unchanged) | — |

Exam-specific rule: review findings contain answer keys. **Never render exam findings or responses in any learner-visible note before grading.** Store them only in `ScholarExam.review`. After grading, append them collapsed to the answer key note (`renderExamAnswerKey`) as `> [!note]- Question review`.

## 4. Runaway-loop prevention (the core of this plan)

Implement every row. Each has a test.

| # | Loop source | Guard | Where | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Review → rewrite → review | One pass per target. A second `lessonComplete` after responses commits with **zero** reviewer requests | `tool-controller.ts` notes path; delete `MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS` and `reserveReview`, replace with `passCompleted(targetKey)` | Integration: blocking finding → author responds → commit; assert request count unchanged |
| L2 | Retrying failed checks | One automatic retry per packet inside the pass, then commit-with-warning | `review-layer.ts` `runReviewPass` | Unit: packet fails twice → receipt has `failure`, lesson commits with warning callout |
| L3 | Author repeating rejected Scholar calls (LaTeX repair, gaps, wrong IDs) | Circuit breaker: **8 consecutive** Scholar tool results with tone `retry` or `error` in one activation → `stopDelivery`. Any success resets the counter. Keep `MAX_PREREVIEW_REJECTIONS = 4` | `tool-controller.ts` `execute` wrapper (count after computing `tone`) | Integration: 8 invalid `notes` calls → 8th stops and aborts; 9th returns the latch message |
| L4 | Unbounded work per activation | Action budget: **250** Scholar tool calls per explicit activation, then `stopDelivery` with the continue hint. Reset only in `resetTransientState` | `tool-controller.ts` | Unit with injected counter |
| L5 | Hung provider (no bytes) | Stall watchdog: abort a reviewer request if **no stream event for 180 s** (`REVIEW_STALL_MS`). Resets on every stream event | `review-runtime.ts` inside `observe()` and around `stream.result()`; for `registry.complete` without a stream use the same timer | Unit: provider never yields → `failure.code = "timeout"` within the injected stall time |
| L6 | Endless reasoning | Output cap from the model: `maxOutputTokens = min(model.maxTokens, 128_000)`; `maxTotalOutputTokens = 2 × that`; keep a **45-minute** per-request backstop (`REVIEW_BACKSTOP_MS`) | `learn-review.ts`/`review-layer.ts` limits; `review-runtime.ts` `DEFAULT_REVIEWER_LIMITS` | Unit: model with `maxTokens: 384000` gets 128000; with 8192 gets 8192 |
| L7 | Wall-clock stops killing progress | **Remove** `LEARN_WORK_LIMIT_MS`, `MIN_REVIEW_WINDOW_MS`, the preparation budget code, the coordinator 20-minute interval and the 12-minute shared review deadline. Replace with L5, L6 and a progress watchdog: stop preparation if **no successful Scholar action and no model stream activity for 15 minutes** of active turn time | `tool-controller.ts`, `runtime-coordinator.ts`, `review-layer.ts` | Update the three existing budget/deadline tests to assert the new behavior |
| L8 | Author wandering with Pi tools | While a Scholar mode is active, active tools = `scholar` + `scholar_quiz` only. Save the previous list on activation and restore it exactly on `deactivateSession` / close / `session_shutdown` | `runtime-coordinator.ts` `syncActiveTools` | Real-extension harness: after `/scholar learn`, active tools exclude `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`; after `/scholar close`, the original list returns |
| L9 | Chat or extension input clearing a stop | Keep: only `resetTransientState` (a Scholar command) clears the latch and counters | already in `captureOpenResponse` | Keep existing test |
| L10 | Question review loops | One pass per question id: author fixes or declines, then the question is shown. No second review | `tool-controller.ts` `reviewQuestion`, `index.ts` `tool_call` hook | Integration: blocking question finding → response → question saved, no second request |
| L11 | Checkpoint write storms | Keep coalescing and `close()` before approval | already done | Keep existing test |

Invariants to assert in tests:

- No code path runs more than one review pass per target per activation.
- A stop is cleared only by an explicit Scholar command.
- Every pass ends: each packet ends by verdict, failure, stall (L5) or backstop (L6).
- A failed or unfinished pass never approves silently. It commits only with a visible warning.

## 5. Any-model compatibility

| Issue | Change | File |
|---|---|---|
| Output limit | L6 | `learn-review.ts` / `review-layer.ts` |
| Chatty models | `parseReviewerVerdict`: if strict parse fails, extract the **last balanced `{...}` object** containing `"status"` and validate it. If none, allow **one** follow-up turn in the same conversation with user message `Return only the JSON verdict object.` (set `maxTurns: 2` for prepared packets) | `learn-quality.ts`, `review-runtime.ts` |
| Text-only models | Visual packets run as text: include captions, equations and the page text; skip images; add an `advice` finding `Figures were not visually checked (text-only model).` and a commit warning. Do not fail configuration | `review-layer.ts`, `learn-review.ts` `reviewOne` |
| Small context windows | Derive sizes: `contextWindow < 64_000` → source window 2 pages, visual packet 2 images; otherwise 4 pages and 6 images | Learn planner |
| Undeclared limits | If `model.maxTokens` is missing, use 16 000; if `contextWindow` is missing, use 32 000 | `review-runtime.ts` configuration check (replace the hard failure) |

Test with simulated models in `tests/verify-scholar-learn-review.mjs`:
- one that wraps the JSON in prose
- one that returns prose first, then JSON on the follow-up turn
- one with `input: ["text"]`
- one with `contextWindow: 32000`
- one with no `maxTokens`

## 6. Exam callouts (keep and finish)

Already implemented; do not rewrite the paper format. Preserve exactly:
- the frontmatter identity fields and `answer_format: checkboxes-v1`
- `<!-- scholar:answer:ID:start -->` / `<!-- /scholar:answer:ID:end -->` markers with a single `> ` frame
- `<!-- scholar:choice:N -->` rows
- `EXAM_PAPER_COMPLETE` as the last marker
- the `## Submit` section and command block outside callouts
- `/scholar exam "ID" submit` confirmation (`submitExam`)
- learner-owned papers never being rewritten (`ensureExamAnswerNote`)

Tasks:
1. **Round-trip test.** Add to `tests/verify-scholar-obsidian-exam.mjs`: create a paper for single choice, select-all and open questions; assert each question heading line starts with `> [!question] Question N`, and each answer region is inside it. Then check one box and type an open answer inside the callout, and assert `parseExamResponses` returns them and `submitExam` succeeds.
2. **Legacy notes.** Assert that `renderExam` for an old exam produces no `### Question` headings, so stale status notes are cleaned up on the next projection.
3. **Exam review findings** stay out of the paper and the exam status note (section 3.3). Test: build an exam with a blocking finding and a response; assert neither the paper nor `renderExam` output contains the finding text; after grading, `renderExamAnswerKey` contains it inside a collapsed callout.

## 7. Phases

Run the full suite and the TypeScript comparison at the end of every phase.

1. **Loop guards first (L3–L9).**
   - Files: `tool-controller.ts`, `review-runtime.ts`, `runtime-coordinator.ts`, `index.ts`.
   - Update the existing tests named "The total Learn deadline…", "The controller enforces the preparation budget…" and "One shared deadline…" to the stall/progress model.
2. **Model compatibility (section 5).**
3. **One pass for Learn (L1, L2, L10).**
   - Change the gate in `lesson.ts`/`learn-quality.ts`; add `findingResponses`; add the commit warning callout in the lesson render (`render/section.ts`).
   - Update integration tests that expect repeated rounds ("third unresolved content review", "Chat and extension input cannot reset the review-round cap") to the one-pass behavior.
4. **Shared layer.** Extract `review-layer.ts`; add Tutor explanation and question packets.
5. **Exam review and callout tests (sections 3.3 and 6).**
6. **Docs, version, install.**
   - Update `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` in three sentences or fewer per change. Bump to 0.6.0 in `package.json` and `npm-shrinkwrap.json`.
   - Commit, then fast-forward the installed copy: `git -C <installed> fetch <working> feat/loading-progress && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD`.
   - Run `node tests/run.mjs --preflight` in the installed copy, plus the three review verifiers.
   - Tell the user to run `/reload` in Pi.

## 8. Final acceptance

- Full suite passes; TypeScript diagnostics unchanged.
- A real-extension replay (Pi's `loadExtensions` against a temporary copy of the vault's `Scholar` folder) shows:
  - `/scholar learn "9.3"` shows the reopen prompt
  - "continue" starts one turn
  - active tools are only Scholar's
  - `/scholar close` restores tools
- Simulated end-to-end Learn run: write → one pass with one blocking finding → response → commit, with exactly one set of reviewer requests.
- Offer the user one real run on a copy of 9.3 with DeepSeek before relying on it.

## 9. Do not

- Add a model as the final "approver". Scholar's code decides commit; models only produce findings.
- Re-review after fixes, or add rounds back.
- Reintroduce fixed wall-clock stops.
- Show exam keys, rubrics or review findings before submission.
- Rewrite existing answer papers, lesson text or deleted content.
- Change teaching guidance, the selected model or the reasoning level.

`runReviewPass(options, packets)` does exactly what `reviewLearnDraft` does today: pool of `REVIEW_CONCURRENCY` workers, packet-key cache, `onCheckpoint`, one aggregate receipt per role. Keep `reviewOne` as the single-packet runner.

### 3.2 One-pass flow (every mode)

```
author writes -> code validators -> ONE review pass -> author answers every blocking finding -> commit
```

- **Finding key.** Compute, don't store: `findingKey = sha256(role + "\u0000" + target + "\u0000" + issue).slice(0, 12)`. The review result shows each finding as `[F-<key>]`. No change to the `ReviewFinding` schema.
- **Author response.** New optional `findingResponses: Array<{ key: string; action: "fixed" | "declined"; note: string }>` on `notes` (Learn and Tutor) and `exam_build` (Exam). Add it to `tool-contract.ts` `ScholarParams`. `note` must be 1–600 characters.
- **Commit rule.** Commit when:
  - a completed pass exists for this target (any content hash), and
  - every blocking finding from that pass has a response, and
  - the code validators pass on the current content.

  Never run a second pass for the same target in the same activation.
- **Execution failures.** A packet that fails (provider error, timeout, output limit, malformed verdict) is retried once, within the same pass. If it fails again, the pass completes anyway, and the commit adds a visible warning, for example `> [!warning] Not independently reviewed: visual (provider error)`.
- **Storage.**
  - Learn: keep receipts in `learnQuality.reviews`, and add `learnQuality.responses?: FindingResponse[]`.
  - Tutor: add `review?: { version: 1; receipts: ReviewReceipt[]; responses: FindingResponse[] }` on `TutorSession`.
  - Exam: add the same field on `ScholarExam`.
  - Validate all three in `state-schema.ts`, updating `hasOnlyKeys` lists and adding an `isFindingResponse` guard in `learn-quality.ts`.
- **Legacy.** Sections already approved under the old gate stay approved. `lessonReady` accepts either the old receipts or the new one-pass record.

### 3.3 Packets per mode

| Mode | Trigger | Packets | Blocks until done? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Learn lesson | `notes.lessonComplete` | Existing crew (`planReviewAssignments`), unchanged | Yes |
| Learn/Tutor question | new graded question (`assess` pending, `scholar_quiz`) | 1 `assessment` packet (question + its source pages + crops) | Yes |
| Tutor explanation | first `notes.lesson` save of a unit | 1 `teaching` packet: that unit's markdown + its `sourcePages` text. At most 1 per unit | Yes, one request only |
| Exam form | `exam_build` | 1 `assessment` packet per question (question, key, rubric, its source pages) + 1 `teaching` packet for the whole form (coverage, balance, cues across questions; no source text) | Yes, before freezing |
| Exam grading | `exam_grade` | none (unchanged) | — |

Exam-specific rule: review findings contain answer keys. **Never render exam findings or responses in any learner-visible note before grading.** Store them only in `ScholarExam.review`. After grading, append them collapsed to the answer key note (`renderExamAnswerKey`) as `> [!note]- Question review`.

## 4. Runaway-loop prevention (the core of this plan)

Implement every row. Each has a test.

| # | Loop source | Guard | Where | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Review → rewrite → review | One pass per target. A second `lessonComplete` after responses commits with **zero** reviewer requests | `tool-controller.ts` notes path; delete `MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS` and `reserveReview`, replace with `passCompleted(targetKey)` | Integration: blocking finding → author responds → commit; assert request count unchanged |
| L2 | Retrying failed checks | One automatic retry per packet inside the pass, then commit-with-warning | `review-layer.ts` `runReviewPass` | Unit: packet fails twice → receipt has `failure`, lesson commits with warning callout |
| L3 | Author repeating rejected Scholar calls (LaTeX repair, gaps, wrong IDs) | Circuit breaker: **8 consecutive** Scholar tool results with tone `retry` or `error` in one activation → `stopDelivery`. Any success resets the counter. Keep `MAX_PREREVIEW_REJECTIONS = 4` | `tool-controller.ts` `execute` wrapper (count after computing `tone`) | Integration: 8 invalid `notes` calls → 8th stops and aborts; 9th returns the latch message |
| L4 | Unbounded work per activation | Action budget: **250** Scholar tool calls per explicit activation, then `stopDelivery` with the continue hint. Reset only in `resetTransientState` | `tool-controller.ts` | Unit with injected counter |
| L5 | Hung provider (no bytes) | Stall watchdog: abort a reviewer request if **no stream event for 180 s** (`REVIEW_STALL_MS`). Resets on every stream event | `review-runtime.ts` inside `observe()` and around `stream.result()`; for `registry.complete` without a stream use the same timer | Unit: provider never yields → `failure.code = "timeout"` within the injected stall time |
| L6 | Endless reasoning | Output cap from the model: `maxOutputTokens = min(model.maxTokens, 128_000)`; `maxTotalOutputTokens = 2 × that`; keep a **45-minute** per-request backstop (`REVIEW_BACKSTOP_MS`) | `learn-review.ts`/`review-layer.ts` limits; `review-runtime.ts` `DEFAULT_REVIEWER_LIMITS` | Unit: model with `maxTokens: 384000` gets 128000; with 8192 gets 8192 |
| L7 | Wall-clock stops killing progress | **Remove** `LEARN_WORK_LIMIT_MS`, `MIN_REVIEW_WINDOW_MS`, the preparation budget code, the coordinator 20-minute interval and the 12-minute shared review deadline. Replace with L5, L6 and a progress watchdog: stop preparation if **no successful Scholar action and no model stream activity for 15 minutes** of active turn time | `tool-controller.ts`, `runtime-coordinator.ts`, `review-layer.ts` | Update the three existing budget/deadline tests to assert the new behavior |
| L8 | Author wandering with Pi tools | While a Scholar mode is active, active tools = `scholar` + `scholar_quiz` only. Save the previous list on activation and restore it exactly on `deactivateSession` / close / `session_shutdown` | `runtime-coordinator.ts` `syncActiveTools` | Real-extension harness: after `/scholar learn`, active tools exclude `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`; after `/scholar close`, the original list returns |
| L9 | Chat or extension input clearing a stop | Keep: only `resetTransientState` (a Scholar command) clears the latch and counters | already in `captureOpenResponse` | Keep existing test |
| L10 | Question review loops | One pass per question id: author fixes or declines, then the question is shown. No second review | `tool-controller.ts` `reviewQuestion`, `index.ts` `tool_call` hook | Integration: blocking question finding → response → question saved, no second request |
| L11 | Checkpoint write storms | Keep coalescing and `close()` before approval | already done | Keep existing test |

Invariants to assert in tests:

- No code path runs more than one review pass per target per activation.
- A stop is cleared only by an explicit Scholar command.
- Every pass ends: each packet ends by verdict, failure, stall (L5) or backstop (L6).
- A failed or unfinished pass never approves silently. It commits only with a visible warning.

## 5. Any-model compatibility

| Issue | Change | File |
|---|---|---|
| Output limit | L6 | `learn-review.ts` / `review-layer.ts` |
| Chatty models | `parseReviewerVerdict`: if strict parse fails, extract the **last balanced `{...}` object** containing `"status"` and validate it. If none, allow **one** follow-up turn in the same conversation with user message `Return only the JSON verdict object.` (set `maxTurns: 2` for prepared packets) | `learn-quality.ts`, `review-runtime.ts` |
| Text-only models | Visual packets run as text: include captions, equations and the page text; skip images; add an `advice` finding `Figures were not visually checked (text-only model).` and a commit warning. Do not fail configuration | `review-layer.ts`, `learn-review.ts` `reviewOne` |
| Small context windows | Derive sizes: `contextWindow < 64_000` → source window 2 pages, visual packet 2 images; otherwise 4 pages and 6 images | Learn planner |
| Undeclared limits | If `model.maxTokens` is missing, use 16 000; if `contextWindow` is missing, use 32 000 | `review-runtime.ts` configuration check (replace the hard failure) |

Test with simulated models in `tests/verify-scholar-learn-review.mjs`:
- one that wraps the JSON in prose
- one that returns prose first, then JSON on the follow-up turn
- one with `input: ["text"]`
- one with `contextWindow: 32000`
- one with no `maxTokens`

## 6. Exam callouts (keep and finish)

Already implemented; do not rewrite the paper format. Preserve exactly:
- the frontmatter identity fields and `answer_format: checkboxes-v1`
- `<!-- scholar:answer:ID:start -->` / `<!-- /scholar:answer:ID:end -->` markers with a single `> ` frame
- `<!-- scholar:choice:N -->` rows
- `EXAM_PAPER_COMPLETE` as the last marker
- the `## Submit` section and command block outside callouts
- `/scholar exam "ID" submit` confirmation (`submitExam`)
- learner-owned papers never being rewritten (`ensureExamAnswerNote`)

Tasks:
1. **Round-trip test.** Add to `tests/verify-scholar-obsidian-exam.mjs`: create a paper for single choice, select-all and open questions; assert each question heading line starts with `> [!question] Question N`, and each answer region is inside it. Then check one box and type an open answer inside the callout, and assert `parseExamResponses` returns them and `submitExam` succeeds.
2. **Legacy notes.** Assert that `renderExam` for an old exam produces no `### Question` headings, so stale status notes are cleaned up on the next projection.
3. **Exam review findings** stay out of the paper and the exam status note (section 3.3). Test: build an exam with a blocking finding and a response; assert neither the paper nor `renderExam` output contains the finding text; after grading, `renderExamAnswerKey` contains it inside a collapsed callout.

## 7. Phases

Run the full suite and the TypeScript comparison at the end of every phase.

1. **Loop guards first (L3–L9).**
   - Files: `tool-controller.ts`, `review-runtime.ts`, `runtime-coordinator.ts`, `index.ts`.
   - Update the existing tests named "The total Learn deadline…", "The controller enforces the preparation budget…" and "One shared deadline…" to the stall/progress model.
2. **Model compatibility (section 5).**
3. **One pass for Learn (L1, L2, L10).**
   - Change the gate in `lesson.ts`/`learn-quality.ts`; add `findingResponses`; add the commit warning callout in the lesson render (`render/section.ts`).
   - Update integration tests that expect repeated rounds ("third unresolved content review", "Chat and extension input cannot reset the review-round cap") to the one-pass behavior.
4. **Shared layer.** Extract `review-layer.ts`; add Tutor explanation and question packets.
5. **Exam review and callout tests (sections 3.3 and 6).**
6. **Docs, version, install.**
   - Update `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` in three sentences or fewer per change. Bump to 0.6.0 in `package.json` and `npm-shrinkwrap.json`.
   - Commit, then fast-forward the installed copy: `git -C <installed> fetch <working> feat/loading-progress && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD`.
   - Run `node tests/run.mjs --preflight` in the installed copy, plus the three review verifiers.
   - Tell the user to run `/reload` in Pi.

## 8. Final acceptance

- Full suite passes; TypeScript diagnostics unchanged.
- A real-extension replay (Pi's `loadExtensions` against a temporary copy of the vault's `Scholar` folder) shows:
  - `/scholar learn "9.3"` shows the reopen prompt
  - "continue" starts one turn
  - active tools are only Scholar's
  - `/scholar close` restores tools
- Simulated end-to-end Learn run: write → one pass with one blocking finding → response → commit, with exactly one set of reviewer requests.
- Offer the user one real run on a copy of 9.3 with DeepSeek before relying on it.

## 9. Do not

- Add a model as the final "approver". Scholar's code decides commit; models only produce findings.
- Re-review after fixes, or add rounds back.
- Reintroduce fixed wall-clock stops.
- Show exam keys, rubrics or review findings before submission.
- Rewrite existing answer papers, lesson text or deleted content.
- Change teaching guidance, the selected model or the reasoning level.

# Scholar handoff — 13 September 2026

## The job that remains

Basam needs Scholar's Learn mode to reliably produce a faithful, understandable, attractive replacement for a textbook section in Obsidian. Griffiths section 9.3 repeatedly took close to an hour without finishing, including when merely reopened. We shipped recovery protections, but **we have NOT demonstrated satisfactory full-section generation speed or successful approval of 9.3**. Do not mistake a timeout that stops correctly, passing mock tests, or a successful tiny model probe for solving that remaining problem.

Latest user request: summarize enough context for a fresh AI to continue. Do not resume editing merely because this document includes suggested next steps; follow the next user's request.

## User priorities and boundaries

- Pi terminal is the message/input surface; Obsidian holds the actual learning material and visible study history. Scholar should be inactive until explicitly opened.
- Quality matters more than token cost, but 30–60 minutes without a completed lesson is unacceptable. User wants honest progress and elapsed timers.
- Teach from the selected PDF faithfully. Explain unfamiliar terms, physical meaning, assumptions, derivation steps and connections. Avoid compressed jargon summaries, shallow explanations and walls of unrelated figures.
- Native Obsidian callouts frame questions, central equations and figures. Keep a question and its associated figure together. Place figures next to explanations; walk through them when useful.
- Central equations use expanded Key equation callouts with rendered math, symbol definitions, assumptions, meaning and source pages. Intermediate algebra need not be boxed. Obsidian math uses `$...$` / `$$...$$`, not raw `\(...\)` / `\[...\]`. Symbol definitions use arrows, not repeated “is” or conjunction “and.” Diagrams should be centered. Dark Obsidian appearance is preferred. Mermaid is optional when helpful.
- Completed sections can be practiced without losing earned progress. Resume the exact unanswered question. Deleted questions/content in visible notes must not be resurrected from hidden history.
- Vault notes are authoritative; no external hidden knowledge store. Existing local configuration can point to the vault. Preserve user edits, source ownership, content hashes and assessment safeguards.
- Pi supports many providers. Avoid model-specific architecture. The installed configuration during testing used **openai-codex / gpt-5.6-luna / max**. User sometimes calls it Lua; logs/settings identified Luna. Do not silently replace the selected model or weaken scientific approval to make timing look better.
- Discover and Research Studio were abandoned/removed. Do not bring them back. Scholar, the rolling-cat loader and themes are separate; the current problem is Scholar.
- Earlier authorization covered fixing/testing Scholar, pushing GitHub and updating the installed copy. Do not disrupt a running Pi/Obsidian study session or regenerate study notes without considering current user intent. Our latest acceptance tests were read-only against an in-memory copy.

## Exact environment and repository state

Windows, PowerShell, America/New_York. Working directory:
`C:\Users\basam\Documents\Codex\2026-09-09\w`

Working Git checkout:
`C:\Users\basam\Documents\Codex\2026-09-09\w\outputs\pi-scholar-loading-progress`
Branch: `feat/loading-progress`.

Installed extension Git checkout:
`C:\Users\basam\.pi\agent\extensions\scholar`
Branch: `main`.

GitHub: https://github.com/BasamAhmed640/pi-scholar

Both checkouts and GitHub main were verified at **66eca3a82a56eceeb0e811c18dfd6efd3e5186c0**, package **0.5.2**, with clean working trees. Commit title: `Fix Learn reopening and bound interrupted review recovery`.
Previous release: 0.5.1, commit `4b672b74264fc00598580891283b54575221d7fe`.

Installed Pi SDK: **0.85.1** at:
`C:\Users\basam\AppData\Local\pi-node\current\node_modules\@earendil-works\pi-coding-agent`
Node:
`C:\Users\basam\AppData\Local\pi-node\current\node.exe`
Pi AI dependency is nested under the SDK's `node_modules\@earendil-works\pi-ai`; do not assume a top-level install. `tests/sdk.mjs` handles discovery/Jiti aliases.

Running Pi instances need `/reload` after their active run ends or is interrupted. A Git pull does not replace an already loaded extension. We did not reload or terminate the user's running session. At last investigation it had switched from 9.3 to 1.1; verify current state before acting.

## Source and vault locations

Vault: `C:\Users\basam\Desktop\Basam's_Vault`

9.3 note:
`C:\Users\basam\Desktop\Basam's_Vault\Scholar\Books\Griffiths E&M\Sections\9.3 - Electromagnetic Waves in Matter.md`

PDF: `C:\Users\basam\Desktop\SIPI_Silicon\Griffiths_E&M.pdf`

Book ID/source hash:
`987099eccd1cb67fc2ea5565ff193a37245576730f944e349b11174900f63826`

9.3 section ID: `chapter-009-section-003`; PDF viewer pages **420–430**.
Sections **1.1, 4.3 and 9.3** have been the user's quality/stress-test examples. Do not assume their current notes have passed a fresh scientific audit.

## What the engine currently does

The main Pi agent writes the lesson, using Scholar's source and persistence tools. On `notes.lessonComplete=true`, three isolated reviewers run: **source fidelity**, **teaching/explanation**, and **visual/math**. They are separate model conversations, not three additional lesson writers. They use the selected Pi model and supported thinking level. A separate assessment reviewer checks a proposed new learner question later. There are at most three simultaneous review requests; the question reviewer does not normally run concurrently with initial lesson approval.

Learn source review uses batches of up to **8 pages**. Visual review uses packets with at most **6 images**, including whole pages and associated current crops. Roles run concurrently; batches within a role run sequentially. Teaching reviews the full lesson with source text. Source and visual batches still receive the **whole lesson/checklist as context**. That broad repeated context and maximum reasoning effort remain plausible latency contributors; do not present them as conclusively isolated causes.

Approval requires complete evidence and passing current-hash reviews. Missing evidence, transport errors, timeout, malformed output and context limits are execution failures, not approval. Content findings can be blocking or optional advice. Mastery is separate from lesson delivery and still requires learner evidence.

Relevant files in either checkout:

- `index.ts`: Pi lifecycle/input hooks and terminal completion state.
- `runtime-coordinator.ts`, `loading-progress.ts`: activation, loading widget, timer, input lock and total Learn deadline.
- `commands.ts`, `command-syntax.ts`: saved-draft reopening and explicit `continue`.
- `tool-controller.ts`: tool dispatch, review orchestration, round limits, stop latch and approval persistence.
- `review-runtime.ts`: isolated model runner, provider/auth selection, evidence preparation, streams, cancellation, limits and safe diagnostics.
- `learn-review.ts`: role prompts, source/visual batching, prepared evidence, cache/reuse and assessment review.
- `learn-quality.ts`: review receipt/schema/approval validation.
- `lesson.ts`, `equation-presentation.ts`, `lesson-figures.ts`, `tool-actions/learning.ts`, `tool-contract.ts`: validated lesson writes and exact patches.
- `policies.ts`: lead writer's instructional and recovery contract.
- `storage.ts`, `note-storage.ts`, `book-service.ts`: authoritative note storage, mutations and projection.

## Diagnosis of the original long attempts

Recorded runs spent many minutes reviewing, hit provider errors/timeouts, rewrote the entire draft, invalidated successful checks, and reviewed again. The old three-review-round limit rejected later review requests but did not itself stop the author from continuing to rewrite. Reopening an unapproved draft automatically restarted preparation. A single equation/figure correction previously required a full structured lesson rewrite.

The parent context was observed around **186k/272k (~68%)**, so parent context exhaustion was not established. A visual reviewer separately hit a context/output allowance. Real scientific findings also existed, including distinctions between signed field amplitudes and nonnegative peak magnitudes; simply bypassing reviewers would be unsafe for teaching quality.

Original log timing totals were approximately 47m24s for one attempt and 23m28s for a later resume, with ~44m40s in review calls. **Those are elapsed session durations, NOT continuous model-processing durations**: Windows sleep occurred during some intervals. Earlier wording calling all 71 minutes “active” was too strong and has been corrected in the release report.

Session file:
`C:\Users\basam\.pi\agent\sessions\--C--Users-basam--\2026-09-13T20-05-05-241Z_01a09c5f-9659-7689-b744-8676a867de60.jsonl`

## Shipped in 0.5.2

1. Reopening a saved unfinished lesson shows its Obsidian location and starts **zero generation**. Explicit `/scholar learn "9.3" continue` starts preparation. Pending questions retain normal resume behavior. The command reports the note path; do not claim it necessarily navigates the Obsidian window.
2. Learn reviewers receive required text/pages/crops upfront. Each batch makes **one verdict request with no tools**, avoiding model turns spent fetching evidence. Assessment review retains its scoped tool loop. Evidence loading uses the same cancellation/deadline budget and fails closed if incomplete.
3. Execution failures persist the returned review receipts, then abort Pi's author loop and latch further Scholar actions off (status remains available). The third unresolved content-review round also actively stops authoring. A new explicit input/activation clears the latch. This prevents automatic retry/full-rewrite cycles.
4. A **12-minute shared review-round deadline** and **20-minute total new-Learn work ceiling** apply. The total clock excludes learner input. The author ceiling also covers writing/repairs. OS suspension cannot execute timers; model/evidence boundaries recheck elapsed wall time to reject overdue buffered responses on resume.
5. `lessonPatch.calloutEdits` can replace one complete equation callout through its structured equation definition, or one figure via new `snapshotId` + `replacesSnapshotId`. Exact old callout and current content hash are required. Other prose/callouts are preserved; history, scope, rendering validation and review invalidation remain enforced. Update affected coverage/figure inventory too.
6. Stream activity reports reasoning/verdict liveness without logging its text. Safe receipt diagnostics store elapsed time, model/tool counts and token usage when available. Raw provider errors/credentials are withheld; known failure categories are retained. Missing usage on incomplete streams is not evidence of zero actual tokens.
7. Final runner requests Pi's standard **`transport: "sse"`** option. The installed SDK documents that providers supporting multiple transports honor it and others ignore it. This is provider-neutral and avoids WebSocket use for one-shot reviews. Selected model and reasoning effort were not changed.

Important limitation: the 20-minute ceiling is a recovery guard, not a promise that lessons finish in 20 minutes. Total-operation interruption can preserve the draft while discarding an in-flight review transaction; do not claim every partial reviewer result is checkpointed continuously. Review receipts are normally persisted after the review call returns. Successful saved batches are reusable only while relevant hashes remain unchanged.

## What testing actually proved

- Full `npm test`: **55 packaged verifiers passed, zero failed**. Most use simulated providers, but exercise actual production controllers, Pi SDK, Poppler, vault codecs and disposable files.
- After the final SSE preference change, reran **20 reviewer-runtime checks** and **17 Learn review integration checks**, all passed.
- Tests include noncooperating provider timeouts, cancellation, late verdicts, wall-clock jumps, current-note edits, deleted/stale content, all source/crop evidence, review reuse, exact callout patches, third-round stopping, zero-generation reopening, progress deadlines, exam behavior and unanswered-question recovery.
- Installed copy passed `npm run test:preflight` after update.
- Package dry-run passed (~448 kB compressed, 119 files), no added runtime dependencies.
- The broad optional TypeScript check still has **55 pre-existing diagnostics**, unchanged after normalization for paths/line shifts. Do not claim a clean typecheck. Address separately if useful; no new diagnostics were introduced.

Live tests, all read-only against a copy of the saved draft:

**First full-review test:** started 22:00:16 UTC, Windows entered Modern Standby 22:07:59, resumed around 22:58:24. All roles returned timeout after apparent 58 minutes. This is NOT a valid speed benchmark. Power events verified sleep; no persistent power settings were changed.

**Awake full-review test (before final SSE preference):** temporarily inhibited idle sleep only for that benchmark process, then restored it. Returned at **720 seconds**. Teaching connection failure at **401 seconds**. Source was still emitting reasoning events when it hit the deadline, without finishing its first source batch. Visual completed one batch, then timed out during batch two of three. **No full lesson approval.** This proves the bounded deadline works and identifies active prolonged reasoning plus transport failure; it does not prove acceptable generation performance.

**Final SSE probe:** one narrow claim from the real PDF page, same Luna/max, completed with a valid pass in **21 seconds**. This proves the final transport/auth/runner can complete a small grounded request. It does NOT certify 9.3, full review speed or a full writer-plus-review cycle.

**No full 9.3 run has been validated on the final SSE version.** This is the most important outstanding acceptance gap.

## Suggested next investigation (not yet implemented)

1. Read the shipped code and the compact release report. Reproduce against an in-memory copy or isolated test vault; inspect current user activity before touching live notes.
2. Run one bounded full 9.3 review on final SSE, recording per-role/batch start/end, input size, available usage and failure category. Keep the machine awake during the measurement without permanently changing settings. Do not log private reasoning, credentials or raw transport payloads.
3. Distinguish model generation time from source preparation, queueing, network failures, repairs and OS suspension. A progress animation alone is not evidence of useful progress.
4. If broad reviews still overrun, investigate **smaller genuinely scoped review assignments/context** and scheduling. Current sequential role batches repeatedly include the entire lesson/checklist. Preserve global coherence and complete source coverage; do not blindly truncate evidence or create more agents without measuring the effect.
5. Consider explicit reviewer reasoning configuration only with clear user-facing semantics. Maximum reasoning on every supporting check may be a poor latency tradeoff, but this was not benchmarked against alternatives. Do not assert that a stronger/cheaper model will fix it or silently downgrade the selected settings.
6. Avoid full rewrites after infrastructure failures. Retry unchanged saved work and reuse valid checks. Investigate whether more incremental checkpointing is warranted when the overall author deadline interrupts a review, while preserving stale-edit/approval protections.
7. Before declaring the problem solved, obtain a complete representative Learn result, then assess scientific fidelity, pedagogical explanations, equation rendering, figure placement, learner-question validity and actual end-to-end time. The user plans to provide feedback on sections 1.1, 4.3 and 9.3.

## Local diagnostic artifacts

All paths below are under:
`C:\Users\basam\Documents\Codex\2026-09-09\w\outputs`

- `scholar-0.5.2-release-report.md` — concise shipped result and limitations.
- `scholar-9.3-hour-long-run-diagnosis.md` — initial diagnosis; interpret its duration totals with the sleep correction above.
- `diagnose-scholar-051.mjs`, `scholar-051-diagnosis.json` — extracted prior session data.
- `inspect-scholar-stall-051.mjs`, `scholar-stall-051-timeline.json` — prior timing analysis.
- `scholar-prepared-live.mjs` — actual-draft review harness; does not save the copied book.
- `scholar-prepared-live-awake.log` — metadata-only awake review events.
- `scholar-prepared-live\2026-09-13T23-03-23-115Z\report.json` — awake full-review result.
- `scholar-prepared-live\2026-09-13T22-00-16-696Z\report.json` — sleep-interrupted first result.
- `scholar-sse-smoke.mjs`, `scholar-sse-smoke.log`, `scholar-sse-smoke-result.json` — final narrow SSE acceptance probe.
- `scholar-052-full-tests-final.log`, `scholar-052-runtime-final.log`, `scholar-052-integration-final.log`, `scholar-052-pack.log` — validation logs.
- `scholar-next-release-tsconfig.json`, `scholar-next-release-baseline-types.log`, `scholar-052-types-final.log` — static baseline comparison.

The first live harness originally called unsupported `runtime.dispose()` after writing its report; that test-harness cleanup mistake was subsequently removed. It was not a Scholar runtime failure. The later awake run and SSE probe exited successfully.

Avoid dumping the diagnostic JSON or session JSONL wholesale: fields contain huge lesson/source text. Parse and select only needed metadata. Keep private study material and logs out of GitHub. Public repository changes include synthetic tests, not the user's textbook content.

No new background agents or benchmarks were left running at handoff. No applicable repository AGENTS.md was found during this work; recheck if the next workspace changes.

## What the engine currently does

The main Pi agent writes the lesson, using Scholar's source and persistence tools. On `notes.lessonComplete=true`, three isolated reviewers run: **source fidelity**, **teaching/explanation**, and **visual/math**. They are separate model conversations, not three additional lesson writers. They use the selected Pi model and supported thinking level. A separate assessment reviewer checks a proposed new learner question later. There are at most three simultaneous review requests; the question reviewer does not normally run concurrently with initial lesson approval.

Learn source review uses batches of up to **8 pages**. Visual review uses packets with at most **6 images**, including whole pages and associated current crops. Roles run concurrently; batches within a role run sequentially. Teaching reviews the full lesson with source text. Source and visual batches still receive the **whole lesson/checklist as context**. That broad repeated context and maximum reasoning effort remain plausible latency contributors; do not present them as conclusively isolated causes.

Approval requires complete evidence and passing current-hash reviews. Missing evidence, transport errors, timeout, malformed output and context limits are execution failures, not approval. Content findings can be blocking or optional advice. Mastery is separate from lesson delivery and still requires learner evidence.

## Shipped in 0.5.2

1. Reopening a saved unfinished lesson shows its Obsidian location and starts **zero generation**. Explicit `/scholar learn "9.3" continue` starts preparation. Pending questions retain normal resume behavior. The command reports the note path; do not claim it necessarily navigates the Obsidian window.
2. Learn reviewers receive required text/pages/crops upfront. Each batch makes **one verdict request with no tools**, avoiding model turns spent fetching evidence. Assessment review retains its scoped tool loop. Evidence loading uses the same cancellation/deadline budget and fails closed if incomplete.
3. Execution failures persist the returned review receipts, then abort Pi's author loop and latch further Scholar actions off (status remains available). The third unresolved content-review round also actively stops authoring. A new explicit input/activation clears the latch. This prevents automatic retry/full-rewrite cycles.
4. A **12-minute shared review-round deadline** and **20-minute total new-Learn work ceiling** apply. The total clock excludes learner input. The author ceiling also covers writing/repairs. OS suspension cannot execute timers; model/evidence boundaries recheck elapsed wall time to reject overdue buffered responses on resume.
5. `lessonPatch.calloutEdits` can replace one complete equation callout through its structured equation definition, or one figure via new `snapshotId` + `replacesSnapshotId`. Exact old callout and current content hash are required. Other prose/callouts are preserved; history, scope, rendering validation and review invalidation remain enforced. Update affected coverage/figure inventory too.
6. Stream activity reports reasoning/verdict liveness without logging its text. Safe receipt diagnostics store elapsed time, model/tool counts and token usage when available. Raw provider errors/credentials are withheld; known failure categories are retained. Missing usage on incomplete streams is not evidence of zero actual tokens.
7. Final runner requests Pi's standard **`transport: "sse"`** option. The installed SDK documents that providers supporting multiple transports honor it and others ignore it. This is provider-neutral and avoids WebSocket use for one-shot reviews. Selected model and reasoning effort were not changed.

Important limitation: the 20-minute ceiling is a recovery guard, not a promise that lessons finish in 20 minutes. Total-operation interruption can preserve the draft while discarding an in-flight review transaction; do not claim every partial reviewer result is checkpointed continuously. Review receipts are normally persisted after the review call returns. Successful saved batches are reusable only while relevant hashes remain unchanged.

- Every Learn/Tutor question is one part and answerable in a terminal (a choice, a number, or one short sentence).
- Reopening a section continues it. No dropdown.
- No model reviewers anywhere (Learn, Tutor, Exam, questions).
- Keep the count limits (8 rejections in a row, 250 actions). Remove the 15-minute stall stops.
- LATER, separate task, not now: one flag-only error check after a lesson is saved.

/** Learn ends with a few short questions. Answered, missed or skipped all count. */
export const QUICK_QUESTIONS = 3;

export function answeredQuickQuestions(section: ScholarSection): number {
  return section.attempts.filter(attempt => attempt.grounding?.purpose !== "diagnostic" && attempt.outcome !== "pending").length;
}

export function quickQuestionBlockers(section: ScholarSection): string[] {
  const left = QUICK_QUESTIONS - answeredQuickQuestions(section);
  return section.status === "complete" || left <= 0 ? [] : [`${left} more short question${left === 1 ? "" : "s"}`];
}

/** Learn and Tutor questions are answered in a terminal: one part, short answer. */
export function assertShortQuestion(text: unknown): void {
  const question = typeof text === "string" ? text : "";
  const parts = question.match(/(?:^|\s)\((?:[a-h]|i{1,3}|iv|v)\)\s/gi) || [];
  if (parts.length >= 2) throw new Error("Ask one part at a time. Learn and Tutor questions must be single-part and answerable in a terminal (a choice, a number, or one short sentence). Put multi-part derivations in the lesson as worked examples.");
  if (question.length > 600) throw new Error("This question is too long for a terminal. Keep it under 600 characters with one short expected answer.");
}

export function unansweredQuestionMessage(attempts: AssessmentAttempt[]): string | undefined {
  const pending = unansweredQuestion(attempts);
  if (!pending) return undefined;
  return pending.format === "multiple-choice"
    ? `Unanswered saved question ${pending.id}: ${pending.question} Call scholar_quiz with only resumeAttemptId=${JSON.stringify(pending.id)} to reopen its exact choices. Do not create a replacement question.`
    : `Pending approved open question ${pending.id}: ${pending.question} Present this exact question again and wait for the learner's answer before resolving it with assess. Do not cancel it just because a session ended, and do not prepare another question.`;
}

export function latestAttemptForKind(section: ScholarSection, kind: AssessmentKind): AssessmentAttempt | undefined {
  const candidates = (section.attempts || []).filter((attempt) =>
    attempt.kind === kind
    && questionCountsTowardCompletion(attempt)
    && attempt.outcome !== "pending"
    && attempt.outcome !== "cancelled"
    && attempt.outcome !== "unavailable",
  );
  return candidates.at(-1);
}

/** Any graded attempt the learner made under the current grounded rule. */
function hasResolvedMasteryEvidence(section: ScholarSection): boolean {
  return section.attempts.some((attempt) =>
    attempt.grounding?.purpose === "mastery"
    && attempt.outcome !== "pending"
    && attempt.outcome !== "cancelled"
    && attempt.outcome !== "unavailable");
}

function checksComplete(section: ScholarSection): boolean {
  return requiredChecks(section.requiredChecks).every(
    (kind) => latestAttemptForKind(section, kind)?.outcome === "pass",
  );
}

export function sectionCompletionBlockers(section: ScholarSection, sourceHash?: string): string[] {
  const objectives = section.objectives || [];
  const objectiveSet = new Set(objectives);
  const coveredSet = new Set((section.coveredObjectives || []).filter((objective) => objectiveSet.has(objective)));
  const coverageComplete = objectives.length > 0 && objectives.every((objective) => coveredSet.has(objective));
  const notesComplete = Boolean(section.synthesis?.trim()) && (section.keyPoints?.length || 0) > 0;
  // Existing results remain valid until this section enters the visual-review
  // workflow. New Learn questions require its receipt at the tool boundary.
  const figuresComplete = section.figureCoverage ? Array.from(
    { length: section.endPage - section.startPage + 1 }, (_, index) => section.startPage + index,
  ).every((page) => {
    const entry = section.figureCoverage!.pages.find((item) => item.page === page);
    return entry?.read && entry.viewed && entry.review
      && entry.candidates.every((label) => entry.review!.figures.some((figure) => figure.label === label));
  }) : section.status === "complete";
  // A grandfathered section keeps the completion it earned under the older
  // rule. Coverage and notes are still required: only the mastery-evidence
  // test is waived, and only for work that was already finished.
  return [
    ...(!coverageComplete ? ["teaching coverage for every declared objective"] : []),
    ...(!notesComplete ? ["saved synthesis and key points"] : []),
    ...(!figuresComplete ? ["source-page and figure review"] : []),
    ...(section.legacyLessonCompletion ? [] : [
      ...(!lessonReady(section, sourceHash) ? ["complete saved instructional lesson"] : []),
      ...objectiveMasteryBlockers(section),
    ]),
    ...(section.legacyCompletion === true ? [] : requiredChecks(section.requiredChecks)
      .filter((kind) => latestAttemptForKind(section, kind)?.outcome !== "pass")
      .map((kind) => `${kind} check`)),
  ];
}

/** A pass for one objective never replaces a miss or missing evidence for another. */
export function objectiveMasteryBlockers(section: ScholarSection): string[] {
  if (!isObjectiveChecks(section.objectiveChecks) || section.objectives.some(objective => !section.objectiveChecks!.some(item => item.objective === objective))) return ["mastery plan for every objective"];
  return section.objectiveChecks.flatMap(({ objective, checks }) => checks.filter(kind => {
    const last = latestAttemptForObjectiveCheck(section, objective, kind);
    return last?.outcome !== "pass";
  }).map(kind => `${kind} evidence for: ${objective}`));
}

export function latestAttemptForObjectiveCheck(section: ScholarSection, objective: string, kind: AssessmentKind): AssessmentAttempt | undefined {
  return section.attempts.filter(attempt => attempt.kind === kind && questionCountsTowardCompletion(attempt)
    && !["pending", "cancelled", "unavailable"].includes(attempt.outcome)
    && attempt.grounding!.basis.some(basis => basis.kind === "objective" && basis.value === objective)).at(-1);
}

export function sectionProgressMessage(section: ScholarSection): string {
  const unanswered = unansweredQuestionMessage(section.attempts || []);
  if (unanswered) return `${section.status === "complete" ? "Section complete; this question is practice. " : ""}${unanswered}`;
  if (section.status === "complete") return "Section complete. Stop this lesson here. Any later questions are practice only and do not change earned completion.";
  const remaining = sectionCompletionBlockers(section);
  return `Section ${section.status}. Remaining: ${remaining.join("; ") || "progress reconciliation"}. Resume only the missing work; do not repeat passed checks or claim completion yet.`;
}

/** Once completion is earned, follow-up questions are practice even if a model labels them mastery. */
export function learnQuestionGrounding(section: ScholarSection, grounding: QuestionGrounding): QuestionGrounding {
  return section.status === "complete" ? { ...grounding, purpose: "practice" } : grounding;
}

    .filter(line => line && !/^#{1,6}\s/.test(line) && !/^\[!/.test(line) && !/^<!--.*-->$/.test(line)
      && !/^!?(?:\[\[[^\]]+\]\]|\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\))$/.test(line) && !/^[-*_`~\s]+$/.test(line)).join(" ");
  const normalized = normalizedLabel(visible);
  return !!normalized && ![item.id, item.description, item.objective, item.kind].some(label => normalizedLabel(label) === normalized);
}

/** Derivation mastery needs applied reasoning or calculation, not recall alone. */
export function sourceAssessmentIssues(ledger: readonly SourceCoverageItem[], objectiveChecks: readonly SourceObjectiveCheck[] | undefined): string[] {
  const issues: string[] = [];
  for (const objective of new Set(ledger.filter(item => item.kind === "derivation").map(item => item.objective))) {
    const check = objectiveChecks?.find(item => item.objective === objective);
    if (!check?.checks.some(kind => kind === "application" || kind === "computation")) {
      issues.push(`Derivation objective "${objective}" needs an application or computation check that asks for its reasoning.`);
    }
  }
  return issues;
}

/**
 * Plan mode validates source scope. Delivery mode additionally links each item
 * to a verbatim, non-label excerpt in the actual saved lesson and verifies the
 * relevant saved equation/figure ID. This is evidence integrity, not a word quota.
 */
export function sourceCoverageIssues(value: unknown, context: SourceCoverageContext, options: { delivered?: boolean } = {}): string[] {
  if (!isSourceCoverageLedger(value)) return ["Provide a valid source-coverage ledger with unique IDs and supported fields."];
  const issues: string[] = [];
  const delivered = options.delivered === true;
  if (!value.length) issues.push("Build a source-based coverage plan before completing Learn.");
  for (const objective of context.objectives) {
    if (!value.some(item => item.objective === objective)) issues.push(`Add source coverage for objective: ${objective}`);
  }
  for (const item of value) {
    const prefix = `Source item ${item.id}`;
    if (!context.objectives.includes(item.objective)) issues.push(`${prefix} must name an exact declared objective.`);
    if (item.sourcePages.some(page => page < context.startPage || page > context.endPage)) issues.push(`${prefix} cites a page outside this section.`);
    if (!delivered) continue;
    if (!item.lessonId || !item.evidence) {
      issues.push(`${prefix} needs a lessonId and an exact explanatory excerpt from the saved lesson.`);
      continue;
    }
    // Public lesson input IDs omit the storage prefix; both forms resolve to the
    // same unit. Multiple matches are ambiguous and must not certify coverage.
    const matches = context.lessons.filter(lesson => matchesLessonId(lesson.id, item.lessonId!));
    if (matches.length !== 1) {
      issues.push(`${prefix} must resolve to one current saved lesson unit.`);
      continue;
    }
    const lesson = matches[0]!;
    if (!comparableMarkdown(lesson.markdown).includes(comparableMarkdown(item.evidence))) issues.push(`${prefix} evidence is not an exact excerpt of its saved lesson.`);
    if (!hasBodyEvidence(item.evidence, item)) issues.push(`${prefix} needs explanatory body evidence, not just a heading, label, or figure embed.`);
    if ((item.kind === "equation" || item.equationId) && (!item.equationId || !lesson.keyEquationIds?.includes(item.equationId))) {
      issues.push(`${prefix} needs a designated Key equation ID actually rendered in this lesson unit.`);
    }
    if ((item.kind === "figure" || item.snapshotId) && (!item.snapshotId || !lesson.embeddedSnapshotIds?.includes(item.snapshotId))) {
      issues.push(`${prefix} needs a saved snapshot ID actually embedded in this lesson unit.`);
    }
  }
  if (delivered) issues.push(...sourceAssessmentIssues(value, context.objectiveChecks));
  return [...new Set(issues)];
}

export function unansweredQuestionMessage(attempts: AssessmentAttempt[]): string | undefined {
  const pending = unansweredQuestion(attempts);
  if (!pending) return undefined;
  return pending.format === "multiple-choice"
    ? `Unanswered saved question ${pending.id}: ${pending.question} Call scholar_quiz with only resumeAttemptId=${JSON.stringify(pending.id)} to reopen its exact choices. Do not create a replacement question.`
    : `Pending approved open question ${pending.id}: ${pending.question} Present this exact question again and wait for the learner's answer before resolving it with assess. Do not cancel it just because a session ended, and do not prepare another question.`;
}

export function latestAttemptForKind(section: ScholarSection, kind: AssessmentKind): AssessmentAttempt | undefined {
  const candidates = (section.attempts || []).filter((attempt) =>
    attempt.kind === kind
    && questionCountsTowardCompletion(attempt)
    && attempt.outcome !== "pending"
    && attempt.outcome !== "cancelled"
    && attempt.outcome !== "unavailable",
  );
  return candidates.at(-1);
}

/** Any graded attempt the learner made under the current grounded rule. */
function hasResolvedMasteryEvidence(section: ScholarSection): boolean {
  return section.attempts.some((attempt) =>

    && attempt.outcome !== "pending"
    && attempt.outcome !== "cancelled"
    && attempt.outcome !== "unavailable");
}

function checksComplete(section: ScholarSection): boolean {

export function sectionCompletionBlockers(section: ScholarSection, sourceHash?: string): string[] {
  const objectives = section.objectives || [];
  const objectiveSet = new Set(objectives);
  const coveredSet = new Set((section.coveredObjectives || []).filter((objective) => objectiveSet.has(objective)));
  const coverageComplete = objectives.length > 0 && objectives.every((objective) => coveredSet.has(objective));
  const notesComplete = Boolean(section.synthesis?.trim()) && (section.keyPoints?.length || 0) > 0;
  // Existing results remain valid until this section enters the visual-review
  // workflow. New Learn questions require its receipt at the tool boundary.
  const figuresComplete = section.figureCoverage ? Array.from(
    { length: section.endPage - section.startPage + 1 }, (_, index) => section.startPage + index,
  ).every((page) => {
    const entry = section.figureCoverage!.pages.find((item) => item.page === page);
    return entry?.read && entry.viewed && entry.review
      && entry.candidates.every((label) => entry.review!.figures.some((figure) => figure.label === label));
  }) : section.status === "complete";
  // A grandfathered section keeps the completion it earned under the older
  // rule. Coverage and notes are still required: only the mastery-evidence
  // test is waived, and only for work that was already finished.
  return [
    ...(!coverageComplete ? ["teaching coverage for every declared objective"] : []),
    ...(!notesComplete ? ["saved synthesis and key points"] : []),
    ...(!figuresComplete ? ["source-page and figure review"] : []),
    ...(section.legacyLessonCompletion ? [] : [
      ...(!lessonReady(section, sourceHash) ? ["complete saved instructional lesson"] : []),
      ...objectiveMasteryBlockers(section),
    ]),
    ...(section.legacyCompletion === true ? [] : requiredChecks(section.requiredChecks)
      .filter((kind) => latestAttemptForKind(section, kind)?.outcome !== "pass")
      .map((kind) => `${kind} check`)),
  ];
}

/** A pass for one objective never replaces a miss or missing evidence for another. */
export function objectiveMasteryBlockers(section: ScholarSection): string[] {
  if (!isObjectiveChecks(section.objectiveChecks) || section.objectives.some(objective => !section.objectiveChecks!.some(item => item.objective === objective))) return ["mastery plan for every objective"];
  return section.objectiveChecks.flatMap(({ objective, checks }) => checks.filter(kind => {
    const last = latestAttemptForObjectiveCheck(section, objective, kind);
    return last?.outcome !== "pass";
  }).map(kind => `${kind} evidence for: ${objective}`));
}

export function latestAttemptForObjectiveCheck(section: ScholarSection, objective: string, kind: AssessmentKind): AssessmentAttempt | undefined {
  return section.attempts.filter(attempt => attempt.kind === kind && questionCountsTowardCompletion(attempt)
    && !["pending", "cancelled", "unavailable"].includes(attempt.outcome)
    && attempt.grounding!.basis.some(basis => basis.kind === "objective" && basis.value === objective)).at(-1);
}

export function sectionProgressMessage(section: ScholarSection): string {
  const unanswered = unansweredQuestionMessage(section.attempts || []);
  if (unanswered) return `${section.status === "complete" ? "Section complete; this question is practice. " : ""}${unanswered}`;
  if (section.status === "complete") return "Section complete. Stop this lesson here. Any later questions are practice only and do not change earned completion.";
  const remaining = sectionCompletionBlockers(section);
  return `Section ${section.status}. Remaining: ${remaining.join("; ") || "progress reconciliation"}. Resume only the missing work; do not repeat passed checks or claim completion yet.`;
}

/** Once completion is earned, follow-up questions are practice even if a model labels them mastery. */
export function learnQuestionGrounding(section: ScholarSection, grounding: QuestionGrounding): QuestionGrounding {
  return section.status === "complete" ? { ...grounding, purpose: "practice" } : grounding;
}
